name: Paragraph Structure
description: Examines the length, rhythm, and internal architecture of paragraphs. AI models naturally default to highly uniform, medium-length blocks of text—often structured around a clear topic sentence, supporting evidence, and a concluding summarization—whereas human writers frequently mix very short, punchy paragraphs with longer, meandering ones to control narrative flow.
algorithm: Paragraph Length Variance and Internal Transition Analysis
mechanism: This method isolates each paragraph and analyzes its word count, sentence count, and internal flow (the presence of standard topic and concluding sentences). Large Language Models (LLMs) are optimized for readability and structural safety. Consequently, they suffer from 'structural homogeneity'. When generating essays, blogs, or reports, an AI will almost always produce paragraphs of very similar lengths (e.g., consistently 4-6 sentences, 80-120 words). Furthermore, these paragraphs are rigidly formulaic: they begin with a transitional phrase ('Furthermore,', 'In addition,'), present a concept, and end with a micro-conclusion. This creates a visually 'blocky' and monotonous reading experience. Human writers are far more erratic. A human might write a massive ten-sentence paragraph exploring a complex idea, followed immediately by a single-sentence paragraph for dramatic emphasis. The system calculates a 'Paragraph Monotony Score' by determining the statistical variance in paragraph length and the repetition of rigid internal semantic structures across the entire document.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing essays, blog posts, and articles, identifying 'wall of text' monotony where every paragraph looks and functions exactly the same, a classic hallmark of zero-shot AI generation.
strengths:
• Detects the visual and structural 'fingerprint' of AI writing that persists even if individual words or sentences are rewritten by a human.
• Excellent at identifying low-effort generative content (like SEO spam or automated homework) which relies heavily on standard templates.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives when analyzing highly structured formal writing, such as scientific abstracts, standardized testing essays (e.g., TOEFL/IELTS), or strict corporate summaries where uniformity is mandated.
• Cannot be used on very short texts (less than 3 paragraphs) where variance cannot be established.
• Can be bypassed by prompt engineering that explicitly instructs the AI to vary paragraph lengths drastically.
parameters:
Analysis: Paragraph Segmentation and Internal Structural Mapping
Metric: Variance in Word/Sentence Count and Topic-Sentence Predictability
Output: 0-100 Structural Homogeneity (Monotony) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-80% accuracy. A very strong indicator of 'lazy' AI generation, especially when combined with Sentence Length Variance analysis.

references.title: Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
Jawahar, G. et al. (2020). Automatic Detection of Machine Generated Text: A Critical Survey. COLING.
